attempts.raw_response: The dosage and route of administration depend on the specific medical indication being treated. For gastric ulcer prevention, the typical oral dose is 200 micrograms taken four times daily with meals and at bedtime. When used for postpartum hemorrhage management, dosing may differ significantly and should only be determined by a qualified medical professional. Patients with a history of cardiovascular disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or known allergies to prostaglandins should inform their doctor before starting treatment. Store the medication at room temperature away from moisture and direct sunlight. If you experience severe abdominal pain, prolonged vomiting, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. Never share this medication with others, as it is prescribed specifically for your individual condition.

pair.human_continuation: This type of massage works to contract the uterine muscles, reducing blood loss. This treatment can be performed at any point after your placenta has been delivered, with or without the help of Misoprostol.  As a treatment for postpartum hemorrhage, uterine massage should be performed by an experienced healthcare professional. You can also perform uterine massage on yourself to help get your uterus back into shape after childbirth. During a postpartum hemorrhage, fluid loss is an issue. Your doctor can help replace your fluids using IV fluids. They will also likely administer blood to replenish the blood you lost due to the hemorrhage. This procedure may sound scary, but it's very normal and will help you feel better.
pair.prefix: Discuss this drug with your doctor to decide if and how you should be taking it. Your doctor will consider both your condition and the possible side effects of the drug to decide if it is the best course of treatment for you.  Possible side effects include diarrhea, fever, and shivering. Misoprostol can be administered orally, sublingually, rectally, or vaginally. Ask your healthcare provider about uterine massage, which can be performed to relieve postpartum hemorrhage.
